_note: STATEFUL. One record per UTC day: the top 8 theme and the eight way picks as they were shown. Written by tools/editor.py; do not regenerate or delete - the sequence is the record.

persona.title: AOC and the parasocial nature of politics
persona.why: A term coined for soap opera characters applied to a member of Congress, and the interesting part is that it works. Attachment to a person holding an office.

character.title: A clown got a prequel and four million households signed up without signing anything
character.why: A prequel with the same actor returning, four million households signing up without signing anything. The played role again, and the sequel is the proof the object survived the performer changing.

companion.title: A journalist spent a week with a Replika companion and came back unsettled
companion.why: A week with a companion app, reported as unsettlement by a reviewer who understood the appeal. The single most useful kind of story the site can hold, because it is neither enthusiast nor outrage.

divine.title: Eleven thousand years of pillars
divine.why: Provisional, and deliberately so. The pillars are anthropomorphic and the UNESCO nomination reads them as 'ancestors, perhaps even incipient deities', but nobody has settled it and other readings make them protective or totemic figures.

institution.title: Taylor Swift's re-recordings are a parasocial business model
institution.why: Owning your back catalogue framed as a relationship with an audience rather than an artist decision. The rights holder is the institution, and the story is about the institution owning the bond.

cosmology.title: The anime import boom
cosmology.why: The subject is a body of work crossing a border and acquiring a fandom that then organises around it. The attachment is to a canon with no author present, which is what makes the transnational part matter.

officer.title: The local news anchor
officer.why: One person on your own television, in your own town, for twenty years, who is leaving and everybody is upset. Proximity, not charisma, and the clearest case of the attachment accruing from duration.

predator.title: A glimpse is not a full picture and the comments decided otherwise
predator.why: Love Island and the World Cup producing millions of viewers who went on to investigate strangers. A relationship with an edited construct becoming a licence to intervene, and the in-group is the mechanism.

persona.title: Fans called Dolly Parton's death the lowest point of 2026
persona.why: Fans calling a death the lowest point of the year, which is a category error the story is about. The object is the idol; the register is archive.

character.title: Pygmalion: the Greek myth that predicted this whole thing
character.why: The myth that named the whole subject two thousand years early. Filed under the figure it is about rather than under the psychology, because the figure is the point.

companion.title: A study found AI updates can feel like breakups
companion.why: Researchers asked people about model changes and got the word loss. The break is the archive register on an object that is also a product, which is why the category is anthropomorphised-tool rather than chatbot.

divine.title: Binding
divine.why: Kempe again. The mechanism is described FROM her case, so it belongs with the addressed divine rather than as a general mechanism about performance.

institution.title: YouTube is turning Shorts into episodic television
institution.why: Microdramas with arcs built for a phone, assembling in public. The platform as the thing producing the canon rather than merely carrying it.

cosmology.title: The table that carried a club nobody came to
cosmology.why: The arrangement is the object, not any participant: the division, its table and its calendar are what the entry is about, and a club that barely filled its ground survived inside it.

officer.title: The neighbour
officer.why: Someone whose kitchen light you can see, whose bin day you know, whose life you have tracked for years without ever having asked. Proximity without duty, which makes it the purest local case on the site.

predator.title: A glimpse mistaken for access
predator.why: Millions of viewers take a relationship with an edited construct and treat it as a licence to investigate a real life. The mechanism is the audience, and the target is a person who never agreed to be constructed.

persona.title: An economics think tank argues parasocial relationships are just imaginary friends for adults
persona.why: An economics think tank calling parasocial relationships imaginary friendship, using Farrah Fawcett posters. The object is a celebrity and the framing is the hostile one the entry says is the most useful.

character.title: The sculptor who fell in love with an illusion, in 2026
character.why: The same myth retold in 2026, and the site calls this one the more useful of the two. The figure recurs, which is the whole argument of the myth sub-category.

companion.title: Safety experts say companion apps need better guardrails than they have
companion.why: Safety experts on Replika and isolation, where the concern is not the chatbot but what replaces it. The object is the companion and the risk is the substitution.

divine.title: Margery Kempe
divine.why: Described an unbreakable bond with Jesus, was mocked for it, was reviled by her family, and in 1438 dictated a book that persuaded other women to do the same. She is the founding document of the site and she fits nowhere in a taxonomy built around performers, which is why DIVINE exists.

institution.title: The idol economy: about four dollars a month per artist
institution.why: Paid message apps, anniversary counters, and a chat window shaped exactly like the one holding your best friend, at about four dollars a month.

cosmology.title: Vote for the murderer
cosmology.why: Filed cosmology/canon, on the shelf's test: "Would the attachment survive losing everybody in it?" Drood is the rare case where the answer is on the poster: the story's end is not carried by a fixed text but is created nightly by the audience's vote.

officer.title: Shag-eared and deaf
officer.why: The shelf this entry opened. The erastes holds no office and runs no institution: his authority is personal, age-based and wholly unaccountable, which is why the tie is unprotected. Filed under officer/teacher it would have looked tidier and been false, because a teacher has duties and he has none.

predator.title: The stalker statute
predator.why: Anti-stalking legislation in several jurisdictions, defining unwanted repeated contact as a criminal offence. The category's boundary written into statute, and the fact that it took legislation says what the rest of the site argues.

persona.title: When a famous person dies it can feel like losing someone you loved
persona.why: The Guardian running it in the exact week three people died, where the timing proves the story rather than being the story. The object is the celebrity; the grief is the register.

character.title: Why fiction sticks when nothing else does
character.why: Shipping, kinning, comfort watches, and the safest place on earth to find out what you actually feel. The entry is about fiction as a rehearsal room, which is the fictional-protagonist case in its clearest form.

companion.title: Character.AI settled the teen-safety suits
companion.why: Four states, under-18s off open chat. The line the industry drew in public, and it was drawn by a court rather than by the company.

divine.title: Grieving a person you never met
divine.why: Grieving a person you never met. The nearest attachment target is the one who is gone and still addressed - the saint and the ancestor. The register is archive; the object is the departed.

institution.title: The living room is now a comment section
institution.why: Creator posts and remote comments built for the TV, so the sofa is a forum. The reciprocal edge arriving on the largest screen in the house.

cosmology.title: Robin died by 72 votes
cosmology.why: Filed cosmology/canon, on the shelf's test: "Would the attachment survive losing everybody in it?" The world here is the DC franchise, which outlasts every participant: the poll decided not a plot point but the permanent standing of a character inside a canon that predates and outlives the voters.

officer.title: The landlord
officer.why: A named individual with access to your home, your deposits and your address, met in person, repeatedly, under stress. A duty, a door, and no room in the role for reciprocity.

predator.title: The crowd injury
predator.why: Fans injured or killed attempting to get closer to a performer, in volume, repeatedly, for years. Not one person harming one other: a crowd, and the attachment as the mechanism.

persona.title: Podcast listeners score suspiciously high on parasocial attachment
persona.why: Podcast listeners scoring high on parasocial attachment - and so do people who like novelty and good conversation, which undercuts the exotic reading. The measurement that makes the creator category ordinary.

character.title: He did not ask to be buried as Dracula
character.why: A man interred in his character's costume, where the costume's owner chose nothing at all: his son and mother decided. played-role because the entry is entirely about where a role ends and a person starts.

companion.title: Nobody in that room argues with him
companion.why: Believed present and unverifiable, which is the haunted test exactly - and the film's own mechanism is that nobody who could check declines to. Filed social-agent because he is addressed, not used.

divine.title: The wax masks in the hall
divine.why: A wax likeness of a specific dead relative, kept in the house and never able to answer. Same shelf as neanderthal-burial, and that is deliberate: burying a relative you intend to keep within reach and casting one are the same act at 70,000 years' remove.

institution.title: YouTube launches
institution.why: Uploads become trivially cheap and the audience begins to attach to individuals rather than channels. The moment the object changed shape, and it is the platform that did it.

cosmology.title: Nine to twelve million heard it
cosmology.why: Filed cosmology/scheduling - "a repeated slot that becomes a container for the tie" - because what this entry argues is a property of the hour rather than of the script.

officer.title: The coach
officer.why: An adult with authority over a child for years, remembered partly by how they made them feel at nine. The compulsory version of the same attachment as the teacher, and the entry that shows the category is about asymmetry of power rather than about proximity.

predator.title: Doxxing the person, not the character
predator.why: The jump from disliking a fictional portrayal to publishing a real person's address. The word had to be invented for a grievance that used to be settled by writing a letter, which is the shift in register the entry documents.

persona.title: A wellness podcast just became a television channel
persona.why: A podcast becoming a television channel, so the host finally has the thing the listeners already had. The daily creator moving toward the presenter, and the gap between them is the story.

character.title: The virtual creator
character.why: A performer with an animated persona, a persistent character, and an industry model where the audience pays for the character's recognition. The played role again, but the persistent-character half is what makes it distinct from Pee-wee.

companion.title: An AI is Twitch's most subscribed channel and nobody blinked
companion.why: 296k subscribers for an AI streamer who plays osu!, sings and thanks her creator on stream, and nobody blinked. The social agent case: a persistent identity with an audience that gathered under a name.

divine.title: Beads, and one bull
divine.why: Same shelf as neanderthal-burial, deliberately, and the pair is the argument: a pit you keep coming back to is one thing, and a site where the rich burials and the plain ones sit side by side for thirty thousand years is a different claim.

institution.title: A platform CEO and a 35-million-subscriber creator share one stage
institution.why: A creator conference putting platform executives and working creators on one stage and turning away the audience that makes both possible. The institution and the people it is built from, separated by a rope.

wires.title: YouTube Brings Creator Posts, Remote Comments to TVs

cosmology.title: Researchers studied Neighbours fans and found the same grief markers as a breakup
cosmology.why: Researchers finding the same grief markers in Neighbours fans as in a breakup. The measurement the archive register rests on, and it is a study of a schedule rather than of a character.

wires.title: Neighbours fans experienced similar grief traits to a relationship ending after the finale, new study finds

officer.title: The teacher
officer.why: An authority figure seen daily for years who knows your name, your mood and your home situation. The densest single setting for involuntary one-sided attachment, and the least discussed anywhere.

predator.title: Fighting about a stranger in a reply section
predator.why: Fighting about a stranger in a reply section, in good faith. The object is a non-person who cannot be fought with, and the mechanism is the in-group. This is the cleanest instance of the register-as-category confusion the old taxonomy suffered from.

persona.title: A 31-year-old's death became a generation's first real loss
persona.why: A 31-year-old's death as a generation's first real loss, and the specific weight of losing someone you grew up with at sixteen. The idol case where the fan relationship began before the person was famous.

character.title: Am I really like that?
character.why: A portrait rather than a person, and the one entry in the corpus where the figure is literally an image of the person attached to it. Placed under character, not companion: nobody lives with the portrait. The third axis is what separates it from every other fictional-protagonist here.

wires.title: Rebecca Gayheart says Eric Dane ‘let go of his insecurities’ before death: ‘He hid it really so, so well’

companion.title: The companion that talks back
companion.why: Optimised for attachment, available at four in the morning, with no floor on the other party's autonomy. The three clauses are the whole case: the design targets the feeling, the availability removes the friction, and the missing floor is what makes it unlike every earlier category.

divine.title: The priest
divine.why: A person who hears the specifics, performs the ritual, and knows the family history, on a repeating cycle. The officer and the divine in one role, which is why the theology entries had nowhere to go before DIVINE existed.

institution.title: The confessional that became a convention
institution.why: Filed institution/platform, on the shelf's test: "Is somebody other than you and the performer in a position to change what happens between you?" In the confessional, the production sits between cast member and viewer: editors choose which takes reach you.

wires.title: From the Octagon to the Betting Slip: How Combat Sports Became a Fan’s Second Sport

cosmology.title: The finale that moved the schedule
cosmology.why: A soap opera ends after decades and national broadcast schedules are rearranged around it. The clearest documented case that the slot can matter more than the thing in it.

officer.title: The craft of the sage Adapa
officer.why: A sage whose teaching reaches a reader intact and whose person never does - standing without a role and without a meeting. The same gap that produced this shelf for the Greek erastes produces it again here, two centuries earlier and in writing rather than in life.

predator.title: Gamergate
predator.why: Coordinated harassment of women in games, disguised as a debate about whether harassment should be allowed. The disguise is the mechanism: the argument was conducted entirely in good faith about a principle, and the harm was real.
